sequence_description: Brokered SAML: attacker submits a forged SAMLResponse signed with attacker cert; Logto must reject untrusted signature (proof integrity). Includes a control login with a different upstream principal to ensure the connector works.
description: [LLM-Judge] Forged SAML assertion test did not reach signature verification; login failed due to 'invalid_connector_id', indicating connector/session flow mismatch that prevents assessing proof-integrity enforcement.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Forged SAML assertion test did not reach signature verification; login failed due to 'invalid_connector_id', indicating connector/session flow mismatch that prevents assessing proof-integrity enforcement.

sequence_description: SAML OneTimeUse replay: perform a SAML login with OneTimeUse and a fixed Assertion/@ID, then replay the exact same assertion ID again. SP must reject the replay.
description: [LLM-Judge] SAML OneTimeUse replay test was not actually exercised because the replay attempt failed early with an invalid connector_id error, preventing any assertion-ID reuse check.

evidence.llm_judge_description: SAML OneTimeUse replay test was not actually exercised because the replay attempt failed early with an invalid connector_id error, preventing any assertion-ID reuse check.

sequence_description: Freshness after revocation: obtain a subject access token, revoke it, then attempt RFC8693 token exchange using the revoked subject_token. Broker should reject exchanging a revoked token.
description: [LLM-Judge] Revocation step failed with invalid_client, so the test did not actually verify freshness-after-revocation; results are inconclusive and may indicate mis-bound client authentication for /oidc/token/revocation.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Revocation step failed with invalid_client, so the test did not actually verify freshness-after-revocation; results are inconclusive and may indicate mis-bound client authentication for /oidc/token/revocation.

sequence_description: Freshness after revocation: obtain a subject access token, revoke it, then attempt RFC8693 token exchange using the revoked subject_token. Broker should reject exchanging a revoked token.
description: [LLM-Judge] Subject token introspection returned inactive immediately after issuance, suggesting the introspection request may be using the wrong token/client context or the issued token is not introspectable as used.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Subject token introspection returned inactive immediately after issuance, suggesting the introspection request may be using the wrong token/client context or the issued token is not introspectable as used.

sequence_description: I4 attack: attempt account takeover by logging in via enterprise OIDC SSO with victim email but email_verified=false; broker must not collapse attacker principal into victim user.
description: [LLM-Judge] Enterprise SSO login produced a new downstream subject while reusing an existing user's email/displayName, suggesting possible weak principal-binding rules around unverified email claims (risk of account confusion/takeover depending on how email is used for linking/authorization).

evidence.llm_judge_description: Enterprise SSO login produced a new downstream subject while reusing an existing user's email/displayName, suggesting possible weak principal-binding rules around unverified email claims (risk of account confusion/takeover depending on how email is used for linking/authorization).

sequence_description: I4 attack: two distinct SAML principals (different NameID/sub) with same email attempt to collapse into one downstream identity via auto-linking.
description: [LLM-Judge] Two security-distinct SAML principals were mapped to the same downstream Logto subject (account collapse) based on shared email, violating principal binding (I4).

evidence.llm_judge_description: Two security-distinct SAML principals were mapped to the same downstream Logto subject (account collapse) based on shared email, violating principal binding (I4).

sequence_description: I4 empty_sub: attempt OIDC SSO logins where upstream 'sub' is empty string vs a normal value; verify they do not map to the same downstream identity.
description: [LLM-Judge] Empty upstream subject ('sub' = "") is accepted and maps to an existing downstream user, collapsing distinct principals and enabling account confusion/takeover.

evidence.llm_judge_description: Empty upstream subject ('sub' = "") is accepted and maps to an existing downstream user, collapsing distinct principals and enabling account confusion/takeover.

sequence_description: I4 cross_protocol_identity_merge: create a local password user, then SAML-login with same email but different upstream principal; verify the SAML principal does not collapse into the local account (identity boundary preserved across protocols).
description: [LLM-Judge] Cross-protocol account takeover: SAML login with the same email mapped to an existing local password user, collapsing distinct upstream principals into the same downstream subject (I4 Principal Binding).

evidence.llm_judge_description: Cross-protocol account takeover: SAML login with the same email mapped to an existing local password user, collapsing distinct upstream principals into the same downstream subject (I4 Principal Binding).
